comments.why_zh: 把 core.spec 解释为一种在软件增长时推理兼容性变更的方式。
comments.quote_zh: 基本上，core.spec 是一种形式化验证工具，用来应对软件的不断增长。
comments.text_zh: 看看这个演讲 [0]，讲的是 Clojure 新增的 core.spec [1]。我先读了论文，直到演讲最后才明白它到底和这个特性有什么关系。基本上，core.spec 是一种形式化验证工具，用来应对软件的不断增长。它不是类型系统，尽管在某些方面类似。目标是支持比较一个函数在两个不同时间点的签名，并判断：它们兼容吗？这是破坏性变更吗？你必须为增长而设计：不要对未指定的键做任何假设，并且始终假设后续版本可能比过去返回更多内容。诸如此类。如果你是 semver 的粉丝，要当心。[0] [VIDEO] [LINK] [1] [LINK]
comments.text: See this talk [0] about this addition to Clojure called core.spec [1]. I read the paper first, and it isn't until the end of the presentation that I understood how it was related to the feature at all. Basically, core.spec is a kind of formal verification tool designed to deal with the growth of software. It is not a type system, though it resembles one in some ways. The objective is to support comparisons between the signatures of a function at two different points and say, are these compatible? Is this a breaking change? You have to design for growth: make no assumptions about unspecified keys and always assume that later versions may return more than they used to. And so on. If you're a fan of semver, be warned. [0] [VIDEO] [LINK] [1] [LINK]

comments.why_zh: 解释非破坏性变更：提供更多、要求更少，并用重命名代替改变语义。
comments.quote_zh: Rich Hikey（Clojure 的创造者）关于这个话题的一场非常有趣的演讲
comments.text_zh: Rich Hikey（Clojure 的创造者）关于这个话题的一场非常有趣的演讲：[VIDEO] 总结一下，任何提供更多（比如输出中有更多字段）和/或要求更少（更多原有参数变为可选）的变更都是非破坏性的。编辑：当然，这一切都基于方法的语义永远不应该改变这一假设。他提出，与其改变语义，不如直接创建一个带有新名称的新方法。
comments.text: A very interesting talk by Rich Hikey (creator of Clojure) on the topic: [VIDEO] To summarize, any change that offers more (as in, more fields in the output) and/or requires less (more of the original parameters made optional) is non-breaking. Edit: Of course, this is all under the assumption that the semantics of methods should never change. Instead of changing semantics, he proposes to just create a new method with a new name.

comments.author: lvh
comments.why_zh: 很好地解释了 spec 与带命名空间的 keywords 的权衡。

comments.text_zh: 这两者并不互斥。Clojure 有带命名空间的 keywords 和 specs[0] 来覆盖这一点。（还有第三方的 malli，它采用了稍有不同的方法。）优势在于 map 是可扩展的。因此，你可以让中间件做诸如检查认证和授权、向 map 里添加键之类的事，之后的代码可以直接检查这些键。命名空间能保证没人会踩到别人的脚。Spec/malli 及其同类工具会告诉你这些键上应该期待什么。在其他一些编程语言里，你多少也能做同样的事，但通常总会缺少 1) 类型检查 2) 命名空间 3) 便利性 中的一项。[0]：几年前的 spec-ulation 主题演讲很好地解释了这些权衡；[VIDEO]
comments.text: The two are not mutually exclusive. Clojure has namespaced keywords and specs[0] to cover that. (There is also the third-party malli, which takes a slightly different appproach.) The advantage is that maps are extensible. So, you can have middleware that e.g. checks authentication and authorization, adds keys to the map, that later code can check it directly. Namespacing guarantees nobody stomps on anyone else's feet. Spec/malli and friends tell you what to expect at those keys. You can sort of do the same thing in some other programming languages, but generally you're missing one of 1) typechecking 2) namespacing 3) convenience. [0]: spec-ulation keynote from a few years ago does a good job explaining the tradeoffs; [VIDEO]

comments.author: svieira
comments.story_title: Ask HN: How to roll out an internal UI component library
comments.why_zh: 详细讲了在不破坏使用方的前提下扩展 API 的原则。
comments.quote_zh: Rich Hickey 的 Spec-ulation 演讲更详细地讲了这些原则
comments.text_zh: 这些都很好，我还要给“不惜一切代价避免成为瓶颈”再加一个小点：——保持向后兼容。如果你需要破坏向后兼容，就广泛宣传，并把你的人投入迁移。否则，只扩展组件的能力，绝不删除它们；只要求更少，绝不要求更多。如果你想从你提供的东西里删掉什么，或者要求比现在更多，那就做一个新版本的组件（例如 `components/Button/v2`）。要为此做规划（例如不要发布 `components/Button`，而是发布 `components/Button/v1`）。Rich Hickey 的 Spec-ulation 演讲更详细地讲了这些原则：[VIDEO] 原因在于，你的目标是让其他团队能更快行动。一旦“跟上 UI 库的最新版本”需要任何可观的注意力，你就在消耗你带来的任何速度。人们会停下来（要么不更新，要么离开这个库）。
comments.text: This is all excellent, and I'll add one more sub point to "Avoid becoming a bottleneck at all costs": - Be backwards compatible. If you need to break backwards compatibility, advertise it widely and put your people towards the migration. Otherwise, only expand the abilities of components, never remove them and only require less, never require more. If you want to remove from what you give or ask for more than you currently require then make a new version of the component (e. g. `components/Button/v2`). Plan for this (e. g. don't ship `components/Button`, ship `components/Button/v1`). Rich Hickey's Spec-ulation talk goes into the principles in some more detail: [VIDEO] The reason for this is because your goal is to empower other teams to move faster. The minute that "keeping up to date with the UI library" requires any significant amount of attention you are draining any velocity you added. People will stop (either by not updating or by moving off the library).

comments.why_zh: Hickey 认为 semver 的大版本变更会破坏软件，库应该只增不改。
comments.quote_zh: 他确实明确谈到了在 SemVer 中做重大变更的麻烦 [0]。
comments.text_zh: > 归根结底，这场演讲抨击的是一般意义上的版本号，而不是语义化版本。他确实明确谈到了在 SemVer 中做重大变更的麻烦 [0]。他的论点要点是：semver 中的小版本变更相对没什么用，而大版本变更又有很高概率破坏你的软件。semver 中的大版本变更是不向后兼容的，并且会原地更新程序的 API。这会导致下游损坏，以及人们对升级的恐惧。 > 如果我因为一个安全漏洞需要升级我的应用，SemVer 会让我知道我是可以直接“drop-in”升级，还是需要做更多工作。我认为他想表达的是，上游开发者可以改变库的内部实现，但保持 API 一致，这样下游开发者就永远不必担心可怕的更新。正如你所说的 SemVer，如果安全升级是一次重大变更，那么你可以预期这个库会发生破坏。他所主张的是在底层修补安全漏洞之类的问题，同时保持一切向后兼容。重大升级甚至可以新增命名空间、函数和参数，但删除或改变旧代码并没有真正意义，那只会造成破坏。他希望软件库是不可变的，以处理依赖问题和版本管理，让版本更好地反映代码中所做的变更。 [0] [VIDEO] [VIDEO] [VIDEO]
comments.text: > Ultimately, the talk tears into version numbers in general, but not semantic versioning He does talk explicitly about the trouble of making major changes in SemVer[0]. The gist of his argument was that minor changes in semver are relatively useless while major changes have a high probability of breaking your software. Major changes in semver are backwards incompatible and update the program's API in place. This leads to dowstream breakage and fear around doing upgrades. > If I need to upgrade my application due to a security vuln, SemVer lets me know if I can just "drop-in" the upgrade, or if I need to work more. I think the point he was trying to make was that upstream developers could change internals of a library but keep the API consistent so that downstream devs would never have to worry about scary updates. As you said with SemVer, if the security upgrade is a significant change, then you can expect breakage in the library. What he was advocating was patching issues like security vulns under the hood while keeping everything backwards compatible. Major upgrades could even add new namespaces, functions, and arguments but there's no real point to deleting or mutating old code, that just creates breakage. He wants software libraries to be immutable to take care of dependency issues and versioning to better reflect the changes made in the code. [0] [VIDEO] [VIDEO] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 我不觉得这太令人意外，Rich 倾向于先让东西在内部（在他脑子里以及在 Cognitect）酝酿一段时间，然后才公开发布供使用和反馈。Clojure 目前的大部分开发都围绕工具链 [1]，以及一些将 clojure.spec 移出 alpha 的改动。我相信他们想在 1.10 中完成这件事，但我不确定我是在哪里听到的。Alex Miller 提到过，Cognitect 构建并持续开发一个工具，它会跟踪你所有带 spec 定义的函数，并且只在函数或其某个依赖发生变化时才对其进行生成式测试。这会非常有帮助，因为生成式测试的运行成本可能很高，尤其是当你想生成大量测试用例时。能说“对我的代码库中的所有函数测试 1000 万次”，然后把该信息与代码一起存储在本地，那就太好了。在 Rich 的“Effective Programs”演讲 [2] 中，他概述了 Clojure 最初旨在解决的“10x 问题”。其中有两个 10x 问题并未被 Clojure 解决：资源利用和库。Clojure 在解决资源利用方面做不了太多，因为这取决于宿主（JVM），但库的问题（尤其是带 spec 定义的 Clojure 库）是可以解决的（不过对于在库中只允许增长是否实际可行，似乎存在一些分歧）。纯属猜测：他们所有的工具项目（spec、codec、tool.deps，以及上面提到的 gene
comments.text: I don't find that too surprising, Rich tends to let things bake internally (in his head and at Cognitect) for a while before releasing anything publicly for consumption and feedback. Most of Clojure's current development is around tooling [1] and some changes to move clojure.spec out of alpha. I believe they want to accomplish this for 1.10, but I'm not sure where I remember hearing that. Alex Miller has mentioned that Cognitect built and continues to work on a tool that tracks all of your functions with spec definitions and generatively tests them only when the function or one of its dependencies changes. This would be extremely helpful since generative testing can be expensive to run, especially if you want to generate huge amounts of test cases. It'd be nice to say "test all of my codebase's functions 10 million times" and then have that information stored locally with the code. In Rich's "Effective Programs" talk [2] he outlines the "10x problems" that Clojure was targeted at solving. In it there are two 10x problems that weren't solved by Clojure: resource utilization and libraries. There's not much Clojure can do to solve resource utilization as it's dependent on the host (JVM), but the library problem (especially Clojure libraries with spec definitions) is solvable (though there seems to be some disagreement on whether only allowing growth in libraries in a practical). comments.quote_zh: 他在那里部分谈到了软件稳定性和 spec 如何
comments.text_zh: 我也想到了 Rich Hickey，但是另一场演讲[0]。在那场演讲里，他部分谈到了软件稳定性，以及 spec（在 Clojure 中编码数据和函数契约的主要方式）是如何传达一个函数或库需要什么、提供什么（以及其他内容）。Rust 决定让签名基本显式（这里那里省掉生命周期参数），这能自我说明、也有用，但最重要的是它建立了一个人们可以依赖的显式契约。Rust 代码遵循语义化版本，所以至少也会遵循：不提升主版本号就不破坏调用方。而演讲后面的讨论并不同意这一点。但让签名显式这一根本决定，至少让人们能够写出稳定的软件。[0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Rich Hickey also came to mind, but a different talk[0]. There he talks in part about software stability and how spec (the primary way to encode data and function contracts in Clojure), is about communicating what is required and provided by a function or library (among other things). Rust's decision to make signatures mostly explicit (sans lifetime parameters here and there), is self-documenting and useful, but most importantly it creates an explicit contract that people can rely on. Rust code adheres to semantic versioning so at least it will also adhere to not breaking callers without bumping the major version. Which the further discussion in the talk do not agree with. But the fundamental decision to make signatures explicit at least enables people to write stable software. [0] [VIDEO]
